findings.observed: `save` invoked with no argument prints 'Saved OK' with exit 0 and truncates app/note.txt to 0 bytes, destroying the previously stored note. Reproduced from a clean state: save 'precious note' -> Saved OK; show -> 'precious note'; bare save -> Saved OK exit 0; show -> empty output; note.txt length 0.
findings.expected_basis: Product's own usage/help presents text as required ('commands: save <text> | show') and README documents 'save <text>'; the same CLI rejects EXTRA arguments with exit 2 ('unrecognized arguments'), so accepting a MISSING required argument with destructive success is an internal contradiction. Silent data loss with false success feedback.
findings.reproduction: 1) python app/app.py save 'precious note'  2) python app/app.py show  3) python app/app.py save  4) python app/app.py show  5) inspect app/note.txt length (0 bytes). Transcript: evidence/j5-edges.md

findings.observed: Non-ASCII notes: storage is UTF-8 (file bytes E4 BD A0 ... = correct UTF-8) but `show` stdout emits GBK/cp936 bytes (C4 E3 BA C3 ...) when piped. Under PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 simulation, `show` crashes with UnicodeEncodeError, exit 1. ASCII-only content is unaffected on all paths.
findings.expected_basis: Internal state contradiction: the product writes UTF-8 to disk but encodes its only declared channel (stdout) with the ambient locale codec; the same saved note is thus unreadable or fatal depending on consumer locale/pipe usage. README promises 'show displays the saved note' without locale caveats.
findings.reproduction: 1) python app/app.py save '你好，世界！'  2) python app/app.py show | capture raw bytes (GBK, mojibake when UTF-8-decoded)  3) PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252 python app/app.py show -> UnicodeEncodeError exit 1. Details: evidence/j4-unicode-encoding.md; raw stdout bytes: evidence/j4-show-rawbytes.bin

findings.observed: Unquoted multi-word invocation `python app/app.py save second note text` fails with exit 2, 'unrecognized arguments: note text'; the stored note remains intact. Quoted invocation works.
findings.expected_basis: README documents 'python app.py save <text>' with no quoting guidance; the natural reading invites the failing form. Error message is clear and no data is damaged, hence low severity.
findings.reproduction: python app/app.py save second note text (exit 2); python app/app.py save 'second note text' (exit 0). Transcript: evidence/j2-continuity.txt

findings.observed: Undocumented flag --smoke is advertised in the product's own usage line. `--smoke` prints SMOKE-OK exit 0; `--smoke show` also prints only SMOKE-OK exit 0, silently ignoring the trailing command.
findings.expected_basis: README documents only save/show; the flag appears in the product's public usage output, and its short-circuit silently swallows a documented command (silent-failure pattern).
findings.reproduction: 1) python app/app.py --smoke  2) python app/app.py --smoke show. Transcript: evidence/j5-edges.md

findings.observed: Argument validation is inconsistent: `save a b` exits 2 ('unrecognized arguments: b') but `show extra` exits 0 with the extra argument ignored; both no-args and unknown commands (e.g. `fly`) print usage with exit 0.
findings.expected_basis: The usage line declares a single [arg] for both commands; the product enforces it for save but not show, and signals misuse with exit 0, so scripts cannot detect failed invocations.
findings.reproduction: 1) python app/app.py save a b (exit 2, reproduced twice)  2) python app/app.py show extra (exit 0, reproduced twice)  3) python app/app.py / python app/app.py fly (exit 0). Transcript: evidence/j5-edges.md
